question: Explain what makes a constitution codified rather than merely written.

draft.raw: O1|P2.1,P2.2|codified constitution|material time or condition, or none|A codified constitution is one in which the principles of a polity's governance are encompassed in a single comprehensive document, whereas a written constitution is when these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents. The distinction lies in whether the principles are contained within a single comprehensive document or across multiple documents.

claims.subject: codified constitution
claims.qualifier: material time or condition, or none
claims.text: A codified constitution is one in which the principles of a polity's governance are encompassed in a single comprehensive document, whereas a written constitution is when these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents. The distinction lies in whether the principles are contained within a single comprehensive document or across multiple documents.

references.label: P2.1
references.text: When these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents, those documents may be said to embody a written constitution; if they are encompassed in a single comprehensive document, it is said to embody a codified constitution.

references.label: P2.2
references.text: The constitution of the United Kingdom is a notable example of an uncodified constitution; it is instead written in numerous fundamental acts of a legislature, court cases, and treaties.[2]

rendered: A codified constitution is one in which the principles of a polity's governance are encompassed in a single comprehensive document, whereas a written constitution is when these principles are written down into a single document or set of legal documents. The distinction lies in whether the principles are contained within a single comprehensive document or across multiple documents. [1]
